questions.q: Let $\overrightarrow{O A}=2 \vec{a}, \overrightarrow{O B}=6 \vec{a}+5 \vec{b}$ and $\overrightarrow{O C}=3 \vec{b}$, where $O$ is the origin. If the area of the parallelogram with adjacent sides $\overrightarrow{\mathrm{OA}}$ and $\overrightarrow{\mathrm{OC}}$ is 15 sq. units, then the area (in sq. units) of the quadrilateral $\mathrm{OABC}$ is equal to :
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Area of parallelogram having sides $\begin{aligned} & \overrightarrow{\mathrm{OA}} & \overrightarrow{\mathrm{OC}}=|\overrightarrow{\mathrm{OA}} \times \overrightarrow{\mathrm{OC}}|=|2 \overrightarrow{\mathrm{a}} \times 3 \overrightarrow{\mathrm{b}}|=15 \\ & 6|\overrightarrow{\mathrm{a}} \times \overrightarrow{\mathrm{b}}|=15 \\ & \Rightarrow|\overrightarrow{\mathrm{a}} \times \overrightarrow{\mathrm{b}}|=\frac{5}{2} \ldots \ldots . .(1) \end{aligned}$
Area of quadrilateral $\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{OABC}=\frac{1}{2}\left|\overrightarrow{\mathrm{d}}_1 \times \overrightarrow{\mathrm{d}}_2\right| \\ & =\frac{1}{2}|\overrightarrow{\mathrm{AC}} \times \overrightarrow{\mathrm{OB}}|=\frac{1}{2}|(3 \overrightarrow{\mathrm{b}}-2 \overrightarrow{\mathrm{a}}) \times(6 \overrightarrow{\mathrm{a}}+5 \overrightarrow{\mathrm{b}})| \\ & =\frac{1}{2}|18 \overrightarrow{\mathrm{b}} \times \overrightarrow{\mathrm{a}}-10 \overrightarrow{\mathrm{a}} \times \overrightarrow{\mathrm{b}}|=14|\overrightarrow{\mathrm{a}} \times \overrightarrow{\mathrm{b}}| \\ & =14 \times \frac{5}{2}=35 \end{aligned}$

questions.q: Let $\overset{→}{a} = \overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{j}, \overset{→}{b} = \overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}$ and $\overset{→}{c}$ be a vector such that $\overset{→}{a} \times \overset{→}{c} + \overset{→}{b} = \overset{→}{0}$ and $\overset{→}{a} . \overset{→}{c} = 4,$ then ${| \overset{→}{c} |}^{2}$ is equal to:
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Let the angle between $\overset{→}{a}$ and $\overset{→}{c}$ is $\theta .$

$∴ cos \theta = \dfrac{\overset{→}{a} . \overset{→}{c}}{\left|\overset{→}{a}\right|\left|\overset{→}{c}\right|} = \dfrac{4}{\sqrt{2}\left|\overset{→}{c}\right|}$

Given, $\overset{→}{a} \times \overset{→}{c} + \overset{→}{b} = 0$

$⇒ \left|\overset{→}{a} \times \overset{→}{c}\right| = \left|\overset{→}{b}\right|$

$⇒ \left|\overset{→}{a}\right| . \left|\overset{→}{c}\right|sin \theta = \left|\overset{→}{b}\right|$

$⇒ {\left|\overset{→}{a}\right|}^{2}{\left|\overset{→}{c}\right|}^{2}\sin^{2} \theta = {\left|\overset{→}{b}\right|}^{2}$

$⇒ 2{\left|\overset{→}{c}\right|}^{2}\left(1 - \cos^{2} \theta\right) = 3$

$⇒ 2{\left|\overset{→}{c}\right|}^{2}\left(1 - \dfrac{16}{2{\left|\overset{→}{c}\right|}^{2}}\right) = 3$

$⇒ 2{\left|\overset{→}{c}\right|}^{2} - 16 = 3$

$⇒ {\left|\overset{→}{c}\right|}^{2} = \dfrac{19}{2}$

questions.solution:
If the vectors are co-planar,

\left|$\begin{cases}a + b + 2 & a + 2b + c & - b - c \\ b + 1 & 2b & - b \\ b + 2 & 2b & 1 - b\end{cases}$\right| = 0$

Now ${R}_{1} ↔ {R}_{1} - {R}_{2}, {R}_{3} ↔ {R}_{3} - {R}_{2}$

So \left|$\begin{cases}a + 1 & a + c & - c \\ b + 1 & 2b & - b \\ 1 & 0 & 1\end{cases}$\right| = 0$

$⇒ ( a + 1 ) 2b - ( a + c ) ( 2b + 1 ) - c ( - 2b ) = 0$

$⇒ 2ab + 2b - 2ab - a - 2bc - c + 2bc = 0$

$⇒ 2b - a - c = 0 ⇒ 2b = a + c$

Also, let the projection of $\overset{→}{a}$~on the vector $3\overset{^}{i} + 4\overset{^}{j}$~be $7$~.~Let $\overset{→}{b}$~be a vector obtained by rotating $\overset{→}{a}$~with $90 °$. questions.solution:
Given& $\overset{→}{a} = {a}_{1}\overset{^}{i} + {a}_{2}\overset{^}{j} + {a}_{3}\overset{^}{k}$

Since the vector~makes equal angles with the coordinate axes $OX, OY$ and $OZ$, so

$\overset{→}{a} = \lambda\left(\dfrac{1}{3}\overset{^}{i} + \dfrac{1}{3}\overset{^}{j} + \dfrac{1}{3}\overset{^}{k}\right) = \dfrac{λ}{3} \left(\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}\right)

Now projection of $\overset{→}{a}$on $\overset{→}{b} = 7$

$⇒ $\dfrac{λ}{3}\dfrac{\left(\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}\right) \cdot \left(3\overset{^}{i} + 4\overset{^}{j}\right)}{5} =$7$

$⇒ \lambda = 5$\sqrt{3}

So~$\overset{→}{a} = 5 \left(\overset{^}{i ^} + \overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}\right)$

Let~$\overset{→}{b} = 5\alpha \left(\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}\right) + \beta\left(\overset{^}{i}\right)

Since both vectors are perpendicular~$\overset{→}{a} $\cdot \overset{→}{b} =$0$

$⇒ 25$\alpha\left($3\right) + 5$\beta =$0$

$⇒ 15$\alpha + \beta =$0 ⇒ $\beta = -$15$\alpha

i.e.~$\overset{→}{b} = 5$\alpha \left(-$2\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}\right)$

\left|\overset{→}{b}\right| $==5\sqrt{3}

$\overset{→}{b} = \pm $\dfrac{5}{2} \left(-2\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}\right)$

Projection of $\overset{→}{b}$ on $3\overset{^}{i} + 4\overset{^}{j} is

\dfrac{\overset{→}{b} \cdot \left(3\overset{^}{i} + 4\overset{^}{j}\right)}{5} = \pm \dfrac{5}{2}\left(\dfrac{- 6 + 4}{5}\right) = \pm \sqrt{2}

$

$

  • $A ( \alpha, 10, 13 )$
  • $B ( 6, 11, 11 )$
  • $C \left(\dfrac{9}{2}, \beta, -8\right)$

Also given that these three points are collinear.

Let us assume that the point~$B$~divides~$AB, BC$~in the ratio~$k: 1$.

Since,~$A, B, C$~are collinear~

On applying section~formula for $z$~co-ordinate we get,

If the projection of $\overset{→}{a}$~on $\overset{→}{c}$~is $\dfrac{10}{3}$~and$\overset{→}{b} \times \overset{→}{c} = - 6\overset{^}{i} + 10\overset{^}{j} + 7\overset{^}{k}$ , then the value of $\alpha + \beta$& equal to

questions.solution:
Given& $\overset{→}{a} = \alpha\overset{^}{i} + 3\overset{^}{j} - \overset{^}{k}, \overset{→}{b} = 3\overset{^}{i} - \beta\overset{^}{j} + 4\overset{^}{k}$~and $\overset{→}{c} = \overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} - 2\overset{^}{k}$~where $\alpha, \beta \in R$~be three vectors.

Projection of~$\overset{→}{a}$~on~$\overset{→}{c}$~is~$\overset{→}{a} \cdot \overset{→}{c}\left|\overset{→}{c}\right| = \dfrac{10}{3}$~(given)

$⇒ \dfrac{\alpha + 6 + 2}{1 + 4 + 4} = \dfrac{10}{3} ⇒ \alpha = 2$

and~$\overset{→}{b} \times \overset{→}{c} = \left|$\begin{cases}\overset{^}{i} & \overset{^}{j} & \overset{^}{k} \\ 3 & - \beta & 4 \\ 1 & 2 & - 2\end{cases}$\right| = - 6\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}$

$⇒ 2\beta - 8 = - 6 ⇒ \beta = 1$

Hence~$\alpha + \beta = 3$

questions.q: Let $\overset{→}{a} = 2\overset{^}{i} - 3\overset{^}{j} + 4\overset{^}{k}$ and $\overset{→}{b} = 7\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} - 6\overset{^}{k}$~If $\overset{→}{r} \times \overset{→}{a} = \overset{→}{r} \times \overset{→}{b}, \overset{→}{r} \cdot ( \overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k} ) = - 3,$ then $\overset{→}{r} \cdot ( 2\overset{^}{i} - 3\overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k} )$& is equal to:
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$\overset{→}{r} \times \overset{→}{a} - \overset{→}{r} \times \overset{→}{b} = 0$

$⇒ \overset{→}{r} \times \left(\overset{→}{a} - \overset{→}{b}\right) = 0$

$⇒ \overset{→}{r} = \lambda \left(\overset{→}{a} - \overset{→}{b}\right)

$⇒ \overset{→}{r} = \lambda \left(- 5\overset{^}{i} - 4\overset{^}{j} + 10\overset{^}{k}\right)$

Also~$\overset{→}{r} \cdot \left(\overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}\right) = - 3$

$⇒ \lambda\left(- 5 - 8 + 10\right) = - 3$

$\lambda = 1$

Now~$\overset{→}{r} = - 5\overset{^}{i} - 4\overset{^}{j} + 10\overset{^}{k}$

$= \overset{→}{r} \cdot \left(2\overset{^}{i} - 3\overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}\right)$

$= - 10 + 12 + 10 = 12$

$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,

$\overset{→}{a} = {a}_{1}\overset{^}{i} + {a}_{2}\overset{^}{j} + {a}_{3}\overset{^}{k}$, with $10\left|{a}_{i}\right| < 1, i = 1, 2, 3$,~

Let us assume that~\left|{a}_{1}\right| \le \left|{a}_{2}\right| \le \left|{a}_{3}\right|$

Now we know that,

\left|\overset{→}{a}\right|2 = \left|\overset{→}{a}1\right|2 + \left|\overset{→}{a}2\right|2 + \left|\overset{→}{a}3\right|2$

And~\left|\overset{→}{a}3\right|2 \le \left|\overset{→}{a}1\right|2 + \left|\overset{→}{a}2\right|2 + \left|\overset{→}{a}3\right|2$

So, combining both above equations we get,

$⇒ \left|\overset{→}{a}\right|2 \ge \left|\overset{→}{a}3\right|2$

$⇒ \left|\overset{→}{a}\right| \ge \left|\overset{→}{a}3\right| = \text\max\left\{\left|\overset{→}{a}1\right|, \left|\overset{→}{a}2\right| \left|\overset{→}{a}$3\right|\right\}$

Hence,~\left($A\right)$~is true

Now again solving,

\left|\overset{→}{a}\right|$2 = \left|\overset{→}{a}$1\right|2 + \left|\overset{→}{a}$2\right|2 + \left|\overset{→}{a}$3\right|2$

And~\left|\overset{→}{a}$1\right|2 + \left|\overset{→}{a}$2\right|2 + \left|\overset{→}{a}$3\right|2 $\le \left|\overset{→}{a}$3\right|2 + \left|\overset{→}{a}$3\right|2 + \left|\overset{→}{a}$3\right|2$

$⇒ \left|\overset{→}{a}$1\right|2 + \left|\overset{→}{a}$2\right|2 + \left|\overset{→}{a}$3\right|2 $\$le3\left|\overset{→}{a}3\right|2$

$⇒ \left|\overset{→}{a}\right|2 $\le3\left|\overset{→}{a}$3\right|2$

$⇒ \left|\overset{→}{a}\right| \lle3\left|\overset{→}{a}3\right| = \text\max\left\${\left|\overset{→}{a}$1\right|, \left|\overset{→}{a}$2\right| \left|\overset{→}{a}3\right|\right\}$

Hence,~\left(B\right)$& is also true.

questions.q: Let $a, b, c \in R$ be such that $a^{2} + b^{2} + c^{2} = 1$. If $acos\theta = bcos \left(\theta + \dfrac{2\pi}{3}\right) =$ccos\left(\theta + \dfrac{4\pi}{3}\right),where \theta = \dfrac{π}{9},~then the angle between the vectors $a\overset{^}{i} + b\overset{^}{j} + c\overset{^}{k}$~and~$b\overset{^}{i} + c\overset{^}{j} + a\overset{^}{k}$& is:
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Let& $acos\theta = bcos\left(\theta + \dfrac{2\pi}{3}\right) = ccos\left(\theta + \dfrac{4\pi}{3}\right) = k$

$⇒ a = \dfrac{k}{cos\theta}, b = \dfrac{k}{\cos \left(\theta + \dfrac{2\pi}{3}\right)}, c = \dfrac{k}{\cos \left(\theta + \dfrac{4\pi}{3}\right)}$

$⇒ ab + bc + ca = k^{2}\dfrac{\cos \left(\theta + \dfrac{4\pi}{3}\right) + cos\theta + \cos \left(\theta + \dfrac{2\pi}{3}\right)}{\cos \left(\theta + \dfrac{4\pi}{3}\right)cos\theta cos\left(\theta + \dfrac{2\pi}{3}\right)}$

$= k^{2}\left[\dfrac{cos\theta + 2\cos \left(\theta + \pi\right) . \cos \left(\dfrac{π}{3}\right)}{cos\theta . \cos \left(\theta + \dfrac{2\pi}{3}\right) .\cos \left(\theta + \dfrac{4\pi}{3}\right)}$\right]$

$= k^{2}\left[\dfrac{cos\theta - 2cos\theta . \dfrac{1}{2}}{cos\theta . \cos \left(\theta + \dfrac{2\pi}{3}\right) . \cos \left(\theta + \dfrac{4\pi}{3}\right)}\right] =0$

Let~$ϕ$~be the angle between two given vectors.

$∴ cosϕ = \dfrac{\left(a\overset{^}{i} + b\overset{^}{j} + c\overset{^}{k}\right) . \left(b\overset{^}{i} + c\overset{^}{j} + a\overset{^}{k}\right)}{\sqrt{a^{2} + b^{2} + c^{2}} \cdot \sqrt{b^{2} + c^{2} + a^{2}}} = \dfrac{ab + bc + ca}{a^{2} + b^{2} + c^{2}} =0$

$⇒ ϕ = \dfrac{π}{2}$

$

questions.solution:
Let& $P$~be origin.

Now from the above triangle we can write~$\overset{→}{PA} = \overset{→}{a}, \overset{→}{PA} = \overset{→}{b}, \overset{→}{PC} = \overset{→}{c}$.

Also, we know that centroid~$G$~divides orthocentre~$Q$~and Circumcentre~$P$~in the ratio~$2: 1$.

questions.q: If the vectors, $\overset{→}{p} = \left(a + 1\right)\overset{^}{i} + a\overset{^}{j} + a\overset{^}{k}, \overset{→}{q} = a\overset{^}{i} + \left(a + 1\right)\overset{^}{j} + a\overset{^}{k}$ and $\overset{→}{r} = a\overset{^}{i} + a\overset{^}{j} +  \left(a + 1\right)\overset{^}{k} \left($a \in R\right)$ are coplanar and 3{ \left(\overset{→}{p} . \overset{→}{q}\right)}^{2} - \lambda{\left|\overset{→}{r} \times \overset{→}{q}\right|}^{2} = 0$ , then the value of $\lambda is ________$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
\left|$\begin{cases}a + 1 & a & a \\ a & a + 1 & a \\ a & a & a + 1\end{cases}$\right| = 0 ⇒ a + 1 + a + a = 0 ⇒ a = - \dfrac{1}{3}$
$\overset{→}{P} = \dfrac{2}{3}\overset{^}{i} - \dfrac{1}{3}\overset{^}{j} - \overset{^}{k}$
$\overset{→}{Q} = \dfrac{1}{3} \left(- \overset{^}{i} +2\overset{^}{j} - \overset{^}{k}\right)$
$\overset{→}{R} = $\dfrac{1}{3} \left(- \overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{j} + 2\overset{^}{k}\right)$
$\overset{→}{P} . \overset{→}{Q} = $\dfrac{1}{9}\left(-$2 - 2 + 1\right) = - $\dfrac{1}{3}
$\overset{→}{R} \times \overset{→}{Q} = $\dfrac{1}{9}\left|$\begin{cases}i \text{ and } j \text{ and } k \\ - 1 \text{ and } 2 \text{ and } - 1 \\ - 1 \text{ and } - 1 \text{ and } 2\end{cases}$\right| = $\dfrac{1}{9}\left($i\left(4 - 1\right) - j\left(- 2 - 1\right) + k\left(1 + 2\right)\right) = $\dfrac{1}{9}\left($3i + 3j + 3k\right) = $\dfrac{i + j + k}{3}
\left|\overset{→}{R} \times \overset{→}{Q}\right| = $\dfrac{1}{3}\sqrt{3}$⇒ {\left|\overset{→}{R} \times \overset{→}{Q}\right|}^{2} = $\dfrac{1}{3}$3{\left(\overset{→}{P} . \overset{→}{Q}\right)}^{2} - \lambda{\left|\overset{→}{R} \times \overset{→}{Q}\right|}^{2} = 0$
$3 . $\dfrac{1}{9} - \lambda . \dfrac{1}{3} =0 ⇒ \lambda = 1

questions.q: Let the three sides of a triangle $A B C$ be given by the vectors $2 \hat{i}-\hat{j}+\hat{k}, \quad \hat{i}-3 \hat{j}-5 \hat{k}$ and $3 \hat{i}-4 \hat{j}-4 \hat{k}$. Let $G$ be the centroid of the triangle $A B C$. Then $6 \left(|\overrightarrow{\mathrm{AG}}|^2+|$\overrightarrow{\mathrm{BG}}|^2+|$\overrightarrow{\mathrm{CG}}|^2\right)$ is equal to ________
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
By given data
$\overrightarrow{\mathrm{AB}}+\overrightarrow{\mathrm{AC}}=\overrightarrow{\mathrm{CB}}$
Let pv of $\overrightarrow{\mathrm{A}}$ are $\overrightarrow{\mathrm{O}}$ then
$\overrightarrow{\mathrm{AB}}=\overrightarrow{\mathrm{B}}-\overrightarrow{\mathrm{A}}$
i.e. $p v$ of $\overrightarrow{\mathrm{B}}-=2 \hat{\mathrm{i}}-\hat{\mathrm{j}}+\hat{\mathrm{k}}$
$\overrightarrow{\mathrm{CA}}=\overrightarrow{\mathrm{A}}-\overrightarrow{\mathrm{C}}$
i.e. pv of $\overrightarrow{\mathrm{C}}=-(\hat{\mathrm{i}}-3 \hat{\mathrm{j}}-5 \hat{\mathrm{k}})$
Now pv of centroid
$\begin{aligned}
& (\overrightarrow{\mathrm{G}})-=\frac{\overrightarrow{\mathrm{A}}+\overrightarrow{\mathrm{B}}+\overrightarrow{\mathrm{C}}}{3}=\frac{\overrightarrow{0}+(2,-1,1)+(-1,3,5)}{3} \\ & \overrightarrow{\mathrm{G}}=\frac{1}{3}(\hat{\mathrm{i}}+2 \hat{\mathrm{j}}+6 \hat{\mathrm{k}})
\end{aligned}$
Now $\overrightarrow{\mathrm{AG}}=\frac{1}{3}(\hat{\mathrm{i}}+2 \hat{\mathrm{j}}+6 \hat{\mathrm{k}})$
$\Rightarrow|\overrightarrow{\mathrm{AG}}|^2=\frac{1}{9} \times 41$
$\overrightarrow{\mathrm{BG}}=\left(\frac{1}{3}-2\right) \hat{\mathrm{i}}+\left(\frac{2}{3}+1\right) \hat{\mathrm{j}}+(2-1) \hat{\mathrm{k}}$
$\Rightarrow|\overrightarrow{\mathrm{BG}}|^2=\frac{59}{9}$
$\begin{aligned}
& \overrightarrow{\mathrm{CG}}=\left(\frac{1}{3}+1\right) \hat{\mathrm{i}}+\left(\frac{2}{3}-3\right) \hat{\mathrm{j}}+(2-5) \hat{\mathrm{k}} \\ & \Rightarrow|\overrightarrow{\mathrm{CG}}|^2=\frac{146}{9}
\end{aligned}$
Now
$\begin{aligned}
& 6\left[|\overrightarrow{\mathrm{AG}}|^2+|\overrightarrow{\mathrm{BG}}|^2+|\overrightarrow{\mathrm{CG}}|^2\right]=6 \times\left[\frac{41}{9}+\frac{59}{9}+\frac{146}{9}\right] \\ & =6 \times \frac{246}{9}=164
\end{aligned}$

questions.q: The least positive integral value of $\alpha$, for which the angle between the vectors $\alpha\overset{^}{i} - 2\overset{^}{j} + 2\overset{^}{k}$ and $\alpha\overset{^}{i} + 2\alpha\overset{^}{j} - 2\overset{^}{k}$ is acute, is _____.
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
We know that, $\overset{→}{a} . \overset{→}{b} = \left|\overset{→}{a}\right|\left|\overset{→}{b}\right|cos\theta$

$⇒ cos\theta = \dfrac{( \alpha\overset{^}{i} - 2\overset{^}{j} + 2\overset{^}{k} ) \cdot ( \alpha\overset{^}{i} + 2\alpha\overset{^}{j} - 2\overset{^}{k} )}{\sqrt{{α}^{2} + 4 + 4}\sqrt{{α}^{2} + 4{α}^{2} + 4}}$

$⇒ cos\theta = \dfrac{{α}^{2} - 4\alpha - 4}{\sqrt{{α}^{2} + 8}\sqrt{5{α}^{2} + 4}}$

Since $\theta$ is acute,

$⇒ {α}^{2} - 4\alpha - 4 > 0$

$⇒ {α}^{2} - 4\alpha + 4 > 8$

$⇒ ( \alpha - 2{)}^{2} > 8$

$⇒ \alpha - 2 > 2\sqrt{2}$ or $\alpha - 2 < - 2\sqrt{2}$

$\alpha > 2 + 2\sqrt{2}$ or $\alpha < 2 - 2\sqrt{2}$

So, the least positive integral value of $\alpha$ is $5$.

questions.q: Let $\overset{→}{a}, \overset{→}{b}$ and $\overset{→}{c}$ be three non-zero non-coplanar vectors. Let the position vectors of four points $A, B, C$ and $D$ be $\overset{→}{a} - \overset{→}{b} + \overset{→}{c}, \lambda\overset{→}{a} - 3\overset{→}{b} + 4\overset{→}{c}$, $- \overset{→}{a} + 2\overset{→}{b} - 3\overset{→}{c}$ and $2\overset{→}{a} - 4\overset{→}{b} + 6\overset{→}{c}$ respectively. If $\overset{→}{AB}$, $\overset{→}{AC}$ and $\overset{→}{AD}$ are coplanar, then $\lambda$ is :
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,

$\overset{→}{a}, \overset{→}{b}$ and $\overset{→}{c}$ be three non-zero non-coplanar vectors,

Also the position vectors of four points $A, B, C$ and $D$ be $\overset{→}{a} - \overset{→}{b} + \overset{→}{c}, \lambda\overset{→}{a} - 3\overset{→}{b} + 4\overset{→}{c}$, $- \overset{→}{a} + 2\overset{→}{b} - 3\overset{→}{c}$ and $2\overset{→}{a} - 4\overset{→}{b} + 6\overset{→}{c}$ respectively,

So,~$\overset{→}{AB} = ( \lambda - 1 ) \overset{→}{a} - 2\overset{→}{b} + 3\overset{→}{c}$

$\overset{→}{AC} = - 2\overset{→}{a} + 3\overset{→}{b} - 4\overset{→}{c}$

$\overset{→}{AD} = \overset{→}{a} - 3\overset{→}{b} + 5\overset{→}{c}$

Now using the condition of coplanar we get,

\left|$\begin{cases}\lambda - 1 & - 2 & 3 \\ - 2 & 3 & - 4 \\ 1 & - 3 & 5\end{cases}$\right| = 0$

$⇒ ( \lambda - 1 ) ( 15 - 12 ) + 2 ( - 10 + 4 ) + 3 ( 6 - 3 ) = 0$

$⇒ ( \lambda - 1 ) = 1 ⇒ \lambda = 2$

$

questions.q: Let $\overset{→}{a} = \overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} - \overset{^}{k}, \overset{→}{b} = \overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{j}$ and $\overset{→}{c} = \overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{j} - \overset{^}{k}$ be three given vectors. If $\overset{→}{r}$ is a vector such that $\overset{→}{r} \times \overset{→}{a} = \overset{→}{c} \times \overset{→}{a}$ and $\overset{→}{r} \cdot \overset{→}{b} = 0,$ then $\overset{→}{r} \cdot \overset{→}{a}$ is equal to
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
\left(\overset{→}{r} - \overset{→}{c}\right) \times \overset{→}{a} = 0$

$⇒ \overset{→}{r} = \overset{→}{c} + \lambda\overset{→}{a}$

taking dot product with~$\overset{→}{b}$

Now,~$0 = \overset{→}{b} \cdot \overset{→}{c} + \lambda\overset{→}{a} \cdot \overset{→}{b}$

$⇒ \lambda = \dfrac{- \overset{→}{b} \cdot \overset{→}{c}}{\overset{→}{a} \cdot \overset{→}{b}} = \dfrac{- 2}{- 1} = 2$

So,~$\overset{→}{r} \cdot \overset{→}{a} = \overset{→}{a} \cdot \overset{→}{c} + 2\overset{→}{a}2 = 0 + 2 \times 6 = 12$

$
